question: Which of the following Articles of Part IV of the Indian Constitution has a provision for the separation of Judiciary from the Executive? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 48
Article 51
Article 49
Article 50
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 50

Explanation:
Article 50 of Part IV of the Indian Constitution, under the Directive Principles of State Policy, provides for the separation of the judiciary from the executive. This aims to ensure the independence of the judiciary. Article 48 deals with agriculture and animal husbandry, Article 49 with protection of national monuments, and Article 51 with promotion of international peace. The principle of separation is based on the doctrine of separation of powers, essential for democratic governance.

☛ Article 48 → Agriculture, animal husbandry, and dairy development
☛ Article 49 → Protection of national monuments
☛ Article 51 → International peace and security

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से अलग करने का प्रावधान है? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)

अनुच्छेद 51
अनुच्छेद 49
अनुच्छेद 50

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 50 राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों के अंतर्गत आता है। यह अनुच्छेद न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से पृथक्करण का प्रावधान करता है। इसका उद्देश्य न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करना है। अनुच्छेद 48 कृषि और पशुपालन से, अनुच्छेद 49 राष्ट्रीय स्मारकों के संरक्षण से, और अनुच्छेद 51 अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति से संबंधित है। न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से अलग करने का सिद्धांत शक्तियों के पृथक्करण पर आधारित है, जो लोकतांत्रिक शासन की मूल शर्त है।

question: What is the maximum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, allowed in a state council of ministers as per Article 164? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly
15% of the total strength of the legislative assembly
20% of the total strength of the legislative assembly
12% of the total strength of the legislative assembly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15% of the total strength of the legislative assembly

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the council of ministers of a state shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that state. This provision was added by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act (2003) to limit the size of the government and reduce financial burden. For instance, if a state assembly has 100 members, the maximum number of ministers is 15. This limit applies to all states, including large ones like Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, though exceptions may exist for smaller states under special circumstances. This provision is crucial for controlling the size of the government in a parliamentary system.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ In which year was the 91st Constitutional Amendment enacted? → 2003
☛ Article 164 deals with? → State Council of Ministers
☛ The maximum number of ministers is based on what percentage? → Total strength of Legislative Assembly
☛ The number of ministers cannot exceed what percentage? → 15% of the Legislative Assembly
☛ Which states are exempt from this limit? → Exceptions may apply to small states
question_hi: अनुच्छेद 164 के अनुसार, राज्य मंत्रिपरिषद में मुख्यमंत्री सहित मंत्रियों की अधिकतम संख्या कितनी हो सकती है? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विधान सभा की कुल सदस्य संख्या का 15%

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 164 के अनुसार, किसी राज्य के मंत्रिपरिषद में मुख्यमंत्री सहित मंत्रियों की कुल संख्या उस राज्य की विधान सभा के कुल सदस्यों की संख्या के 15% से अधिक नहीं हो सकती। यह प्रावधान 91वें संविधान संशोधन (2003) द्वारा जोड़ा गया था ताकि सरकार का आकार सीमित रहे और वित्तीय बोझ कम हो। उदाहरण के लिए, यदि किसी राज्य की विधान सभा में 100 सदस्य हैं, तो मंत्रियों की अधिकतम संख्या 15 होगी। हालांकि, यह सीमा उत्तर प्रदेश और महाराष्ट्र जैसे बड़े राज्यों पर भी लागू होती है, लेकिन कुछ राज्यों में विशेष परिस्थितियों में अपवाद हो सकते हैं। यह प्रावधान संसदीय प्रणाली में सरकार के आकार को नियंत्रित करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

question: Dr. BR Ambedkar was appointed as the _____ of independent India in 1947. (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)

question_hi: 1947 में स्वतंत्र भारत में डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर को _____ के रूप में नियुक्त किया गया था। (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: Articles 52 to 78 of the Indian Constitution deal with: (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: the Legislature
the Judiciary
the State Executive
the Union Executive
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the Union Executive

Explanation:
Articles 52 to 78 of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive. These articles cover the President (Articles 52-62), the Vice-President (Articles 63-73), and the Council of Ministers (Articles 74-78). Article 52 states that there shall be a President of India, who is the constitutional head of the nation. Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President. Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and other ministers. Thus, these articles pertain to the executive branch of the central government.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Articles related to President → 52 to 62
☛ Articles related to Vice-President → 63 to 73
☛ Articles related to Council of Ministers → 74 to 78
☛ Article 52 → There shall be a President of India
☛ Article 74 → Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 52 से 78 किससे संबंधित हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)

न्यायपालिका
राज्य कार्यपालिका
केंद्र कार्यपालिका
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है केंद्र कार्यपालिका

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 52 से 78 तक केंद्रीय कार्यपालिका से संबंधित प्रावधान हैं। इसमें राष्ट्रपति (अनुच्छेद 52-62), उपराष्ट्रपति (अनुच्छेद 63-73), और मंत्रिपरिषद (अनुच्छेद 74-78) के पद, शक्तियां और कार्य शामिल हैं। अनुच्छेद 52 कहता है कि भारत का एक राष्ट्रपति होगा, जो देश का संवैधानिक प्रमुख है। अनुच्छेद 74 में मंत्रिपरिषद का प्रावधान है जो राष्ट्रपति को सहायता और सलाह देती है। अनुच्छेद 75 प्रधानमंत्री और अन्य मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति से संबंधित है। इस प्रकार, ये अनुच्छेद केंद्र सरकार के कार्यकारी अंग से संबंधित हैं।

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) mentioned in the Indian Constitution?  (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: DPSP’s are justiciable.
DPSP’s are non-justiciable.
DPSP’s are legally bounded.
DPSP’s are non-amendable.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is DPSP's are non-justiciable.

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution. They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts. DPSPs guide the state in policy-making but do not provide legal remedy if violated. They can be amended by the Parliament. The objective of DPSPs is to establish social and economic justice and promote the concept of a welfare state. They are inspired by the Irish Constitution. The DPSPs are fundamental in governance but not legally binding. They aim to reduce inequality and ensure fair distribution of resources.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Source of DPSP → Constitution of Ireland
☛ Nature of DPSP → Non-justiciable
☛ Amendability of DPSP → Can be amended by Parliament
☛ Objective of DPSP → Social-economic justice and welfare state
☛ Articles in Part IV → 36 to 51

question: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as ________. (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Morley-Minto Reforms
Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms
Ilbert Bill
Pitt’s India Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Morley-Minto Reforms

Explanation:
The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms. This act was enacted during British rule in India, expanding the legislative councils. It introduced communal representation by creating separate electorates for Muslims. The act was named after the then Secretary of State for India Lord Morley and Viceroy Lord Minto. It increased the number of Indian members in legislative councils, but was limited as most members were still appointed by the government. This reform was an attempt to grant partial political rights to Indians. The act also allowed members to ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but control remained with the British. It was a significant step in the constitutional development of India.

☛ What policy was introduced? → Communal representation
☛ Who was the Viceroy? → Lord Minto

question: Which of the following Acts was based on the Mountbatten plan? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Indian Independence Act, 1947
Composition of Constituent Assembly
Simon Commission, 1927
Government of India Act, 1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian Independence Act, 1947

Explanation:
The Mountbatten Plan was announced on 3 June 1947, proposing the partition of India and the creation of two independent dominions (India and Pakistan). To implement this plan, the Indian Independence Act, 1947 was enacted by the British Parliament in July 1947. This Act granted independence to India on 15 August 1947 and dissolved the British suzerainty. The Government of India Act, 1935 was an earlier legislation; the Simon Commission arrived in 1927-28; and the Composition of Constituent Assembly was related to the plan but is not an Act. Thus, the correct answer is the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

question: According to the Indian Constitution, who can remove the members of the State Public Service Commission? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 2)

The President of India
The Chief Minister of the concerned state
The Governor

Explanation:

question: In which year was the 42nd Amendment in the Indian Constitution passed? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1980
1974
1976
1978
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1976

Explanation:
The 42nd Amendment to the Indian Constitution was passed in 1976 during the government of Indira Gandhi. It is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because it brought numerous changes to the basic structure of the Constitution. This amendment added the words socialist, secular, and integrity to the Preamble. It also introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A). It attempted to limit judicial review and enhanced the power of Parliament. The amendment was enacted during the Emergency period (1975-77).

question: With respect to the National Green Tribunal (NGT), which of the following statements is correct regarding the NGT’s jurisdiction and the role of high courts? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: NGT decisions are not subject to judicial review.
NGT has exclusive jurisdiction, and high courts cannot hear cases related to the environment.
NGT is subordinate to the high courts in terms of territorial jurisdiction.
NGT decisions can only be appealed to the Supreme Court, bypassing high courts entirely.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NGT is subordinate to the high courts in terms of territorial jurisdiction.

Explanation:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act. The NGT has jurisdiction over environmental matters, but it is subordinate to the high courts in terms of territorial jurisdiction. This means that while the NGT can hear cases related to the environment across the country, its decisions can be appealed directly to the Supreme Court, bypassing the high courts. However, high courts still retain their power to hear environmental cases under their writ jurisdiction. The NGT's decisions are subject to judicial review, and it is not an exclusive authority; high courts can also hear environmental matters. The NGT consists of a chairperson and judicial and expert members.

question: With regards to the Constitutional Amendment Bill, which of the following is correct? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: It is mandatory to be passed in both houses of Parliament to become an Act.
It is mandatory to be passed in Lok Sabha only to become an Act.
It is mandatory to be passed in Rajya Sabha only to become an Act.
It is mandatory to be passed in either house of Parliament to become an Act.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is mandatory to be passed in both houses of Parliament to become an Act.

Explanation:
According to Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, a Constitutional Amendment Bill must be passed by both houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) with a special majority to become an Act. This procedure ensures that any change to the Constitution is made with broad consensus. After being passed separately by both houses, the bill is sent to the President for assent. For certain amendments, ratification by state legislatures is also required. Thus, passing in only one house is insufficient. The special majority requires more than 50% of the total membership of the house and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Role of President → President's assent is mandatory; cannot withhold it
☛ Word used in Article 368 → 'passed by both Houses'
☛ Types of amendments under Article 368 → Simple majority, special majority, and amendments requiring state consent
☛ First Constitutional Amendment → was done in 1951

question: Which of the following Fundamental Duties instructs a parent to provide opportunities of education to their child between the age of 6 and 14 years? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: The System of dual government (Dyarchy) in the provinces was introduced by which Act of the British Government in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1929
Government of India Act, 1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced the system of dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces. Under this system, provincial subjects were divided into reserved subjects (controlled by the Governor) and transferred subjects (administered by ministers responsible to the legislative council). This Act also established a bicameral legislature at the centre and continued communal representation. It came into effect in 1921 and was a first step towards responsible government at the provincial level.

Explanation:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 (मॉन्टेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार) ने प्रांतों में द्वैध शासन प्रणाली (द्विशासन) लागू की। इसके तहत प्रांतीय विषयों को दो भागों में बांटा गया: सुरक्षित विषय (गवर्नर के नियंत्रण में) और हस्तांतरित विषय (मंत्रियों को सौंपे गए, जो विधान परिषद के प्रति उत्तरदायी थे)। इस अधिनियम ने केंद्र में भी द्विसदनीय विधानमंडल की स्थापना की और सांप्रदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व की व्यवस्था को जारी रखा। यह अधिनियम 1921 से लागू हुआ और इसने प्रांतीय स्तर पर जिम्मेदार सरकार की दिशा में पहला कदम उठाया।
